title: Enterprise Onboarding, Escalation & QBR Playbook (Support + Integrations)
author: Ava Chen
content:
Summary

This playbook combines the canonical enterprise onboarding checklist, the customer success escalation procedure, an integration checklist for common platform integrations (API/SDK, webhooks, VPC), known issues & workarounds, and a repeatable health check / QBR materials template. It is the single-source-of-truth used by Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), and Support for all Tier-1 enterprise customers.

Scope

- Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated, Private, Hosted with enterprise contracts)
- Covers pre- and post-signing onboarding (30/60/90 day plans), in-product integration, escalation paths, and quarterly business review (QBR) materials
- Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks for production incidents; those are referenced in the Appendix

Owners & Participants

- Document owner: Ava Chen (Customer Success)
- Primary teams: Customer Success (owner), Solutions Engineering, Support (SRE escalation), Product (as needed), Security (for VPC/on-prem)
- SLA / escalation owner: Support on-call -> SRE -> Engineering (model/runtime)

Prerequisites

- Signed contract and onboarding order form with agreed deliverables and timelines
- Customer point-of-contact (POC) roster (technical, product, legal/compliance)
- API keys and initial access configured (or private deployment credentials)

30/60/90 Day Onboarding Plan (standardized)

1. Day 0-7: Kickoff & access
   1.1 Kickoff meeting: Introductions, goals, success metrics, timelines, and immediate blockers.
   1.2 Access: Verify API keys, account roles, and when applicable, VPC network peering/whitelisting.
   1.3 Baseline data: Collect sample prompts, expected QPS, and latency targets.

2. Day 8-30: Integration & validation
   2.1 Integration track selection: SDK (Node/Python/Go), REST, or Private deployment.
   2.2 Run basic test cases: generation, chat, embeddings. Capture token counts and latency for each scenario.
   2.3 Security review: Standard data flow diagram and transfer classification. If Private, begin KMS/HSM key exchanges.
   2.4 Health dashboards: Provide initial access to per-route dashboards and cost breakdowns in Redwood Console.

3. Day 31-60: Performance optimization & QA
   3.1 Configure batching/caching recommendations from Redwood Optimize.
   3.2 Validate model quality against customer prompt set (holdout evals).
   3.3 Pilot rollout: Canary 5-10% traffic with monitoring and automatic rollback configured.

4. Day 61-90: Production rollout & QBR prep
   4.1 Full production cutover with staggered ramps and escalation windows.
   4.2 Knowledge transfer: Handover runbooks and on-call contacts to customer operations.
   4.3 First QBR scheduling: Prepare health metrics and roadmap alignment.

Escalation Playbook (for support incidents and customer-impacting issues)

Severity definitions

- Sev-1 (Critical): Platform outage or production API unavailable for >5 minutes, or data leak.
- Sev-2 (High): Major functionality degraded for many users (e.g., sustained high error rate >5% for 15m).
- Sev-3 (Medium): Functionality degraded for subset of traffic or feature regressions affecting UX.
- Sev-4 (Low): Minor bugs, documentation requests, enhancement requests.

Immediate actions (triage checklist)

1. Acknowledge within 15 minutes for Sev-1/2, 4 hours for Sev-3, 1 business day for Sev-4.
2. Gather: customer ID, API keys used, timestamps, request IDs, sample requests, and reproducible steps.
3. Assign owner: Support engineer takes initial ownership and opens internal incident channel (Slack #inc-<customer>-<id>).
4. Communication: Notify customer POC with incident summary, impact, and ETA for next update.

Escalation matrix

- Triage (Support L1) -> Support L2 (specialist) -> SRE on-call -> Eng-serving-runtime -> Product (if design change required).
- Contacts: (kept in PagerDuty) - do not publish PII here. Follow PagerDuty escalation policy 15/30/60.

Post-incident

- Postmortem required for Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents within 3 business days.
- Root cause analysis (RCA) within 7 business days.
- Action items tracked in eng-platform JIRA with assigned owners and ETA.

Integration Guide (API, SDK, Webhook, VPC) - quick checklist

- Pre-integration checklist:
  - Confirm account and API keys
  - Validate allowed IPs and network rules
  - Share sample prompt set and expected QPS

- API/SDK steps:
  1. Install SDK: npm i @redwood/inference or pip install redwood-inference
  2. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY as environment variable
  3. Run integration smoke test: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'
  4. Verify streaming responses and function/tool calling if used

- Webhooks:
  - Provide webhook endpoint TLS configuration and verification token
  - Configure retry policy (exponential backoff) and idempotency keys

- VPC / Private deployment:
  - Exchange network CIDRs and BGP details (if applicable)
  - Provide KMS key ARNs and certificate fingerprint
  - Validate control plane connectivity and audit log ingestion

Configuration matrix (example)

| Integration Type | Minimum Required | Recommended | Typical Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| REST API | API key, TLS | SDK integration, retry middleware | Customer SE |
| SDK | SDK version, env var | pinned SDK + CI smoke tests | Customer Eng |
| Webhooks | HTTPS endpoint | Signed payloads, retries | Customer Eng |
| VPC | CIDRs, firewall rules | KMS + private peering | Customer Cloud Ops |

Known Issues & Workarounds (maintained list)

1. Issue ID: CS-2026-014 - Occasional 503s for long-generation requests
   - Symptom: Intermittent 503 returned when generation exceeds 12s on certain model variants.
   - Workaround: Use streaming response mode, or pin to higher-throughput model variant (e.g., redwood-large-ht).
   - Status: Mitigated in next-runtime release; customer workaround recommended.

2. Issue ID: CS-2025-098 - Webhook duplicate deliveries during transient retries
   - Symptom: Same webhook event received multiple times within 60s window.
   - Workaround: Use idempotency keys and de-duplication on receiver.
   - Status: Platform retries now include Retry-After headers.

3. Issue ID: CS-2026-021 - Embedding dimension mismatch in older SDKs
   - Symptom: SDK returns 1024-dim vectors but model table expects 1536.
   - Workaround: Upgrade to SDK >= 1.4.0 or use server-side conversion utility (see Appendix B).
   - Status: Fixed in SDK 1.4.0

Support Process & SLAs

- Channels: Support portal (primary), email (support@redwood.ai), Slack (partner channels), PagerDuty for on-call emergency.
- Response targets: Acknowledge Sev-1/2 within 15 minutes; provide next-update cadence every 30 minutes until mitigated.
- Resolution windows (best-effort): Sev-1 within 4 hours; Sev-2 within 1 business day; Sev-3 within 3 business days; Sev-4 per roadmap.
- Escalation thresholds: If ETA slips >20% of promised window, escalate to CS Director and notify customer executive sponsor.

Health Checks & QBR Materials (templates and KPIs)

Standard health check (weekly)

- Metrics to review:
  - API availability (30d/7d/24h)
  - Error rate by route (5xx and 4xx breakdown)
  - P95/P99 latency by route and model variant
  - Cost per 1k tokens by route and model variant
  - Cache hit rate and prefix reuse
  - Model-quality drift: eval score on canonical prompt set (monthly)

QBR agenda (60 minutes)

1. Executive summary (5m): top-line health and any major incidents
2. Usage & cost trends (10m): tokens, top routes, anomalies
3. Performance & reliability (10m): SLOs, latency, error trends
4. Quality & product outcomes (15m): prompt-set evals, A/B results, customer feedback
5. Roadmap & open action items (10m): FYI on upcoming runtime/model changes
6. Decisions & next steps (10m): agreement on optimizations, next QBR date

QBR deliverables (delivered 3 days before meeting)

- One-page health summary (PDF)
- Exported dashboards (CSV) for top 10 routes
- Incident summary for any Sev-1/2 events since last QBR
- Proposed optimizations and expected token-cost impact

Appendices

- Appendix A: Links to runbooks and incident playbooks (eng-platform/runbooks, oncall/incident-process)
- Appendix B: SDK upgrade notes and conversion scripts (attach code snippets in Confluence page)
- Appendix C: Contact matrix & PagerDuty policies (internal link to secrets store)

Change log

- 2025-11-15: Created - initial merge of onboarding and escalation docs.
- 2026-03-04: Updated known issues list and QBR templates; clarified Sev definitions and added VPC checklist.

How to use this document

- CS owners: follow the 30/60/90 plan for each enterprise customer and update the checklist when milestones complete.
- Support: use the escalation playbook for triage and ensure post-incident follow-ups are recorded.
- SE/Engineering: reference the integration matrix during pre-sales and onboarding to scope work.

If you find missing items or product changes that invalidate steps here, submit an edit request and add reviewers listed at the top.
